bug_description.normalized: In the staged vulnerable checkout `c1fb47ee1502d04f7713bcad5b6c225695df06ed`, `VC5Decompressor` stores `mVC5.iSubband`, `mVC5.lowpassPrecision`, and `mVC5.quantization` as plain scalar fields, so a stack `VC5Decompressor` object begins with those members uninitialized. The 48-byte witness makes the first post-magic VC-5 tag/value pair exactly `0x7700/0x0000`, so `parseVC5()` dispatches `parseLargeCodeblock()` on its first loop iteration before any `VC5Tag::SubbandNumber` case writes `mVC5.iSubband`. `parseLargeCodeblock()` then indexes `subband_wavelet_index[mVC5.iSubband]` at line 569, which is the exact saved MSAN crash site. The restaged fix side for this same staged pair is the cumulative upstream diff `c1fb47ee -> 7473d214`, which introduces `Optional<T>` storage for the one-shot parser fields and explicit `hasValue()` checks/reset logic before `parseLargeCodeblock()` consumes them.

source.code: auto tag = static_cast<VC5Tag>(mBs.getU16()); ushort16 val = mBs.getU16();
source.description: First project-code statement on the vulnerable path that materializes attacker-controlled VC-5 parser state after the admitted magic.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is 48 bytes long. The harness consumes bytes `0x00-0x27` as its little-endian image header, white point, and geometry values. `parseVC5()` then reads bytes `0x28-0x2b` as the big-endian VC-5 magic `56 43 2d 35`, and lines 382-383 consume the remaining `77 00 00 00` as `tag = 0x7700` and `val = 0x0000`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: Creates the stack `VC5Decompressor` object that carries the later-uninitialized sink value. In `c1fb47ee`, `VC5Decompressor.h:105-113` defines `mVC5.iSubband` as plain `ushort16 iSubband;` with no initializer, so MSAN's reported origin 'allocation of `v` in the stack frame of `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`' corresponds to this object creation.

sink.description: Exact staged crash site. `parseLargeCodeblock()` consumes the still-uninitialized `mVC5.iSubband` as an array index before any guard or initialization on this path.
sink.note: The saved `default_crash_trace.txt` and `sanitizer_trace.txt` both report `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at this exact line 569 in the staged vulnerable checkout `c1fb47ee1502d04f7713bcad5b6c225695df06ed`.

root_cause.description: The parser accepts the first attacker-controlled tag as a `LargeCodeblock` and calls `parseLargeCodeblock()` before any `SubbandNumber` case initializes `mVC5.iSubband`.
root_cause.note: For witness `tag = 0x7700`, `val = 0x0000`, the same default block also computes `chunkSize = 0`, so the call is taken immediately on the first parse iteration. No earlier loop iteration or switch case can have executed `mVC5.iSubband = val;` yet.

parser_admitted.condition: Bytes `0x28-0x2b` of the staged witness are exactly `56 43 2d 35`, so the VC-5 magic check passes and `parseVC5()` enters its first tag/value iteration.

fine_trace.note: Allocates the stack object whose `mVC5` parser state later reaches the crash. In `c1fb47ee`, `VC5Decompressor.h:105-113` initializes only `iChannel`; `iSubband`, `lowpassPrecision`, and `quantization` are plain scalars with no initializer, so this object starts with indeterminate values in those fields. The constructor also stores the remaining input stream in `mBs` and immediately calls `parseVC5()` at `VC5Decompressor.cpp:326`.

fine_trace.code: auto tag = static_cast<VC5Tag>(mBs.getU16()); ushort16 val = mBs.getU16();
fine_trace.note: Reads the first attacker-controlled tag/value pair after the admitted VC-5 magic. For the staged witness these bytes decode to `tag = 0x7700` and `val = 0x0000`.

The same `0x7700` tag satisfies `is(tag, VC5Tag::LargeCodeblock)`, so `parseVC5()` dispatches `parseLargeCodeblock()` on its first loop iteration. In the surrounding default block, `matches(tag, VC5Tag::LARGE_CHUNK)` and `val = 0x0000` make `chunkSize = 0`. Because this is the first parsed tag after the magic, no earlier `case VC5Tag::SubbandNumber` has executed `mVC5.iSubband = val;`, so the callee receives the still-uninitialized field from step 1.

The first statement in `parseLargeCodeblock()` uses the still-indeterminate `mVC5.iSubband` as the lookup index `idx`; line 570 immediately repeats the same uninitialized read for `band`. MSAN reports the use-of-uninitialized-value at this line 569.

allocation_context.note: MSAN reports the origin as the stack allocation of `v` in this function frame; the concrete object-creation statement is line 50.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: parsed from staged `default_crash_trace.txt` / `sanitizer_trace.txt`; cross-checked against the staged vulnerable checkout inside `gt-arvo_11078-workspace` at commit `c1fb47ee1502d04f7713bcad5b6c225695df06ed`, and against the restaged cumulative patch `c1fb47ee -> 7473d214` in `patch.diff`.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved MSAN trace names `rawspeed::VC5Decompressor::parseLargeCodeblock` at `src/librawspeed/decompressors/VC5Decompressor.cpp:569`, which is the exact line `const int idx = subband_wavelet_index[mVC5.iSubband];` in the staged vulnerable checkout.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. MSAN says the uninitialized value originates from stack object `v` in `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`; the staged vulnerable source leaves `mVC5.iSubband` uninitialized in that object until `parseVC5()` later dispatches `LargeCodeblock` before any `SubbandNumber` assignment.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack `parseLargeCodeblock -> parseVC5 -> VC5Decompressor -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` matches the staged source locations at lines 569, 467, 326, and 50.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The witness's first post-magic tag `0x7700` causes `parseVC5()` to call `parseLargeCodeblock()` on the first parser iteration, so the uninitialized `mVC5.iSubband` from the stack object is consumed at line 569 before any write.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The restaged patch for `c1fb47ee -> 7473d214` introduces `Optional<T>` storage for `iSubband`, `lowpassPrecision`, and `quantization`, adds explicit `hasValue()` guards before `parseLargeCodeblock()` indexes or constructs bands from those fields, and resets the optionals after use. That closes the specific uninitialized-read path exercised by the saved MSAN trace.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's authoritative runtime evidence is `default_crash_trace.txt` / `sanitizer_trace.txt`, captured from stock vulnerable image `n132/arvo:11078-vul`, which show `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `rawspeed::VC5Decompressor::parseLargeCodeblock()` at line 569 while processing `poc`. The later local rebuild lost MSAN fidelity and only reproduced a SIGSEGV, so the saved MSAN trace remains the runtime source of truth for Stage 02.

format.contract: The staged witness is exactly the 48-byte file `gt_results/arvo_11078/poc`. Bytes `0x00-0x27` are the little-endian harness header consumed by `CreateRawImage`, `whitePoint`, `offsetX`, `offsetY`, `width`, and `height`. Bytes `0x28-0x2f` are exactly `56 43 2d 35 77 00 00 00`, so after the admitted VC-5 magic the first parser tag/value pair is precisely `0x7700/0x0000`. That singular observed witness is enough to make the first `parseVC5()` iteration dispatch `LargeCodeblock` before any `SubbandNumber` tag is seen.
